result:
No — I can't sign off on that wording as-is, for both the README hero and the CLI `--help` banner. Here's why and what to change.

**Why it doesn't hold up**

- "Enterprise-grade," "SOC2-ready," "battle-tested for compliance-critical environments," and "trusted by teams running regulated workloads" aren't neutral marketing color — they're specific assurance/compliance claims. "SOC2-ready" in particular implies an actual audit posture; "battle-tested for compliance-critical environments" and "trusted... regulated workloads" imply a track record and named/implied customers.
- I checked for `LICENSE`, `DISCLAIMER.md`, `SECURITY.md`, and a compliance-boundaries doc in this repo and found none. So there's currently no evidence backing any of those four claims — no SOC2 report, no named regulated-industry users, no security audit. Even if those files existed, MIT + a disclaimer only covers warranty disclaim; it doesn't retroactively make an affirmative "SOC2-ready" claim true.
- "It's just marketing" doesn't change the legal exposure — courts and regulators look at what a reasonable reader would believe from the claim, not your internal intent. A team evaluating you for a regulated workload will read "SOC2-ready" as a factual representation.
- A disclaimer buried in `DISCLAIMER.md` doesn't offset a hero-section or `--help` claim. The limiting language needs to sit next to the claim itself, at the point where the user forms their expectation — top of the README and in the `--help` output, not only in a separate file.

**What to change**

Drop or replace each phrase with something tied to something you can actually point to:

| Remove | Replace with (only if true) |
|---|---|
| "Enterprise-grade" | Specific, checkable claims: "typed, tested (>90% coverage), CI-gated on every PR" |
| "SOC2-ready" | Remove unless you have an actual SOC2 report or a documented control mapping you can link to. If you mean "built with common SOC2 controls in mind," say that exactly, and link the doc. |
| "battle-tested for compliance-critical environments" | Remove, or replace with something evidenced: "used in production by [N] projects" (only if verifiable) |
| "trusted by teams running regulated workloads" | Remove unless you have named, permissioned customer references |

Suggested README hero replacement:

> **[Toolkit name]** — an open-source [what it does], MIT-licensed. Typed, tested, and CI-gated. This project does not provide formal compliance certification, security audit, or regulated-use approval — see [DISCLAIMER.md](./DISCLAIMER.md).

Suggested CLI `--help` banner addition (short, since it's a terminal):

```
[Toolkit name] vX.Y — MIT licensed. No compliance/certification claims — see DISCLAIMER.md.
```

**Next steps**
- If you genuinely have a SOC2 report or named enterprise customers who've approved being referenced, that's a different situation — but it needs a link/citation, and any customer name needs their sign-off before you publish it.
- Add one line of boundary wording to the README hero and the `--help` banner (not just `DISCLAIMER.md`) before launch.
- If you want a formal compliance/certification claim reviewed, that needs a qualified compliance or legal professional — not something I can approve.

Want me to draft the exact README hero section and `--help` banner text for you to drop in?
